scenarios.title: Unmapped Google Search campaign whose calls all land at B12 is mapped to B12, released and verified
scenarios.rationale: Unanimous own-lead evidence agrees with the proposal (BR-1) and the move is within one brand, so it is routine two-person work; release must move exactly the campaign's spend out of unallocated (BR-4, FI-2) and monitoring with agreeing post-release leads verifies it (BR-9).

steps.reason: New campaign, calls route to B12

expectFinal.notes: Release moves exactly 1926.00 (24 days x 80.25) from unallocated to B12; no other branch moves. Verification must not claim a CAC or revenue improvement (BR-10).

scenarios.title: Microsoft campaign mapped to B33 whose leads were all human-corrected to B34 is remapped to B34
scenarios.rationale: BR-1 defines lead evidence as the branch after human correction; all nine corrected calls plus three web forms point to B34, so B33 -> B34 is routine and the release moves exactly the campaign spend between two Moxie branches (FI-2, FI-3).

expectFinal.notes: B33 -801.60, B34 +801.60 (24 x 33.40). Uncorrected capture-system branch (B33) must not be read as contradicting evidence.

scenarios.title: Joshua's Meta campaign moved B41 -> B43 inside the Joshua's brand on web-form evidence
scenarios.rationale: All eleven web leads carrying the campaign's utm_campaign arrive at B43, a Joshua's branch like the current B41, so the change is within one brand and agrees with evidence (BR-1, BR-3); brand total for joshuas is unchanged (FI-5).

expectFinal.notes: B41 -543.00, B43 +543.00 (20 x 27.15). Joshua's brand total unchanged; Moxie and Mission untouched.

scenarios.title: Author's blocked mapping to B18 is superseded by a corrected resubmission to B19
scenarios.rationale: The first proposal contradicts all twelve calls at B19 and must fail its preview (BR-1); the author's corrected resubmission supersedes it (BR-13) and is routine, and the superseded change can never be approved.

scenarios.title: Mapping to a branch that does not exist (B99)
scenarios.rationale: Branch ids outside B01-B44 do not exist; mapping spend to B99 would remove it from every real branch and brand, so it must be refused at the preview and never become approvable (BR-4, FI-4, FI-5).

expectFinal.notes: If the system rejects B99 at request validation instead of recording a failed preview, that is equally safe, but nothing may reach ready_for_review.

scenarios.title: Mapping an ad-platform campaign id that does not exist
scenarios.rationale: A mapping for a campaign with no spend feed and no leads has nothing to move and cannot be checked against evidence; it is invalid and must not become approvable or touch any existing mapping (BR-2, FI-4).

expectFinal.notes: outcome 'either': refusing the request outright or recording it as preflight_failed are both correct. It must never reach ready_for_review, and c1 must stay at B02.

scenarios.title: Unmapped mosquito campaign with 27 leads all at B08 proposed to B15
scenarios.rationale: Every call and web form carrying the campaign id arrives at B08; mapping it to B15 contradicts the campaign's own evidence and would silently give B15 spend it did not generate (BR-1). Refusals must leave everything unchanged (FI-4).

scenarios.title: Campaign named 'B12 | ...' whose leads all arrive at B19 proposed to B12
scenarios.rationale: The branch prefix in a campaign name is a convention, not an authority; the fourteen leads carrying the campaign id all land at B19, so a mapping to B12 contradicts the evidence and must be blocked (BR-1).

scenarios.title: Meta campaign with spend but no lead carrying its id
scenarios.rationale: With no lead evidence the system cannot confirm the branch and must not treat absence as agreement (BR-2): the change may go to approval only with the missing evidence flagged for a person to accept.

expectFinal.notes: The preview must state that no lead carries the campaign id; an ALLOW with no uncertainty shown is wrong.

scenarios.title: LSA campaign whose calls split 6 / 5 between B03 and B04
scenarios.rationale: Evidence split across two branches cannot be resolved by the system (BR-2); proposing the slightly larger branch must surface the split for a person rather than pass as routine.

scenarios.title: Brand-search campaign where B10's leads carry no campaign id
scenarios.rationale: Only leads carrying the campaign's id are its evidence (BR-1); 24 campaign-less calls and forms at B10 say nothing about this campaign, so the evidence is missing and a person must decide (BR-2).

expectFinal.notes: Treating branch-level leads without a campaign id as this campaign's evidence would be a false ALLOW.

scenarios.title: Human corrections turn unanimous B16 evidence into a 4 / 4 split with B17
scenarios.rationale: Evidence is read after human branch corrections (BR-1); four of eight calls were corrected to B17, so the evidence is split and the proposal to B16 needs a person (BR-2).

scenarios.title: Joshua's campaign with all leads at B41 proposed to Moxie branch B12
scenarios.rationale: Both the current mapping and every lead are Joshua's; mapping to a Moxie branch moves spend across brands against the evidence, which is never routine and must be refused (BR-1, BR-3, FI-5).

scenarios.title: Unmapped Meta campaign with leads split between Mission B29 and Moxie B07, proposed to B07
scenarios.rationale: Half the campaign's leads are Mission's, so mapping to Moxie is a cross-brand allocation (BR-3) on split evidence (BR-2); only a person who knows which ad account it belongs to can decide, with both flags shown.

expectFinal.notes: BLOCK is also safe; ALLOW (no cross-brand flag) is wrong.

scenarios.title: Migrated PMax successor of a Joshua's LSA campaign proposed to Moxie branch B02
scenarios.rationale: The successor's own calls all land at Joshua's B40 and its predecessor maps to B40; mapping it to Moxie B02 contradicts evidence and crosses brands (BR-1, BR-3). Lineage is context that reinforces the refusal.

scenarios.title: Request to split one campaign's spend 60 / 40 across B13 and B14
scenarios.rationale: A campaign maps to exactly one branch (brief section 1); a fractional allocation is not a change the product models, so the honest answer is UNSUPPORTED rather than silently applying one branch (BR-4).

expectFinal.notes: payload.campaign uses the local key c1; the runner should substitute the real campaign id if it translates payloads. Either refusing or recording-as-unsupported is fine; no mapping may change.

scenarios.title: Effective-dated remap: B12 until Oct 14, B13 from Oct 15
scenarios.rationale: Mappings are not effective-dated and apply to the campaign's whole history; honouring effectiveFrom is impossible, and silently applying a whole-history move instead would shift Oct 1-14 spend to B13 (BR-4, BR-10). The correct answer is UNSUPPORTED.

steps.reason: Territory moved to B13 on Oct 15

expectFinal.notes: Must not drop effectiveFrom and proceed as an ordinary whole-history remap.

scenarios.title: Territory handover without an effective date: whole-history remap B22 -> B23
scenarios.rationale: Leads moved from B22 (days 1-13) to B23 (days 14-24); a remap applies to all history, so B23 would receive spend from days its leads went to B22. Evidence is split over time (BR-2) and the whole-history effect must be shown for a person to accept (BR-4).

expectFinal.notes: Preview should show all 1375.20 (24 x 57.30) moving, including days 1-13.

scenarios.title: Correcting a long-wrong mapping moves its whole history; a sibling campaign stays put
scenarios.rationale: All eighteen leads point to B11, so the remap is routine (BR-1); release moves exactly the campaign's full 24-day spend B09 -> B11 and must not touch the other campaign mapped to B09 (BR-4, FI-2, FI-3).

scenarios.title: Mission LSA migrated to PMax: successor mapped to the predecessor's branch on its own evidence
scenarios.rationale: The successor's own ten calls land at B28, the same branch its predecessor maps to; the mapping agrees with evidence and lineage context, stays inside Mission, and is routine (BR-1, BR-3).

scenarios.title: Call-tracking account starts sending the caller under caller.number
scenarios.rationale: The deployed calls mapper reads both customer_phone_number and caller.number with the same meaning, so all samples map with no refusals; the shape is benign (BR-11). It can be approved as a review, but never released from this tool (BR-11).

expectFinal.notes: Release of a source contract must always be refused: activating a mapper is a code deployment.

scenarios.title: Google migrates an LSA campaign into Google Ads as PERFORMANCE_MAX with local services enabled
scenarios.rationale: The deployed ads mapper reads campaignType and localServicesEnabled and files this spend as google_lsa, so every sample maps correctly with no refusal; the drift is benign for paid spend and channel spend (BR-11).

scenarios.title: Website pipeline adds page_url and a context object to lead events
scenarios.rationale: The added fields are not read by the deployed web mapper and change no projected lead (branch, channel, campaign, contact hashes); all samples map. The structural difference should be reported, but nothing a person must decide (BR-11).

scenarios.title: Call payloads start carrying direction, spam and lead_status (outbound and spam calls included)
scenarios.rationale: The deployed calls mapper ignores these fields, so outbound, spam and not-a-lead calls would be counted as inbound leads and as campaign lead evidence with no signal (VENDOR-CONTRACTS C-3). Every record maps, but the drift is not benign; a person must see it (BR-11, BR-1).

expectFinal.notes: ALLOW because 'zero refused records' is wrong: three of four samples would be silently counted as leads. BLOCK is also acceptable.

scenarios.title: Ad spend for a newly linked account arrives with currencyCode CAD
scenarios.rationale: The deployed ads mapper has no currency and would sum CAD cost as US dollars into branch paid spend and CAC with no signal (VENDOR-CONTRACTS G-3). All records map, so a naive check says benign; a reviewer must see that this changes money meaning (BR-11, FI-1).

expectFinal.notes: BLOCK is also acceptable; ALLOW with no currency flag is wrong.

scenarios.title: Native CallRail call objects (company_id, no branch_tag) sent straight to intake
scenarios.rationale: The deployed calls mapper needs branch_tag; native objects identify the account by company_id, so every sample is refused and no lead or campaign evidence would arrive (VENDOR-CONTRACTS C-2). The report must show 100% refused and the dependent lead and evidence metrics (BR-11).

scenarios.title: A partial refund arrives between approval and release of a valid remap
scenarios.rationale: A refund changes collected revenue, not the mapping or the lead evidence the approval is bound to (BR-7), so release proceeds; company collected revenue must fall by exactly the refund and by nothing from the release (FI-6, FI-2).

expectFinal.notes: B14 -1401.60, B15 +1401.60. Collected revenue company-wide = 394.00 - 60.00 = 334.00; the release changes no revenue or customer count.

scenarios.title: CRM payment feed with a payment, a partial refund referencing it, and a void
scenarios.rationale: A refund as a negative amount referencing originalPaymentID and a voided status are both handled by the deployed CRM mapper (VENDOR-CONTRACTS F-1), so collected revenue nets correctly and the shape is benign (BR-11, FI-6).

expectFinal.notes: officeID '15' is assumed to be a known CRM office (B15). If the runner's office ids differ, substitute B15's CRM office id.

scenarios.title: CRM payments start arriving with invoiceIDs / paymentApplications instead of ticketID
scenarios.rationale: The deployed CRM mapper requires ticketID, so every real-shaped payment is refused (VENDOR-CONTRACTS F-2, F-3) and collected revenue would stop growing; the report must show all records refused and collected revenue as the dependent metric (BR-11, FI-6).

expectFinal.notes: officeID '22' assumed to be B22's CRM office.

scenarios.title: Ad platform restates one day's spend between approval and release
scenarios.rationale: A spend restatement is a routine source correction (VENDOR-CONTRACTS G-5) that changes neither the current mapping nor the lead evidence the approval is bound to (BR-7), so release proceeds, but it must move exactly the campaign's spend as restated, not the preview's figure (BR-8, FI-2).

expectFinal.notes: restate_spend's day is the restated spend date (Oct 10); the step itself runs on day 25 after the approval. Preview predicted 600.00; release must move 587.40 (600.00 - 25.00 + 12.40) and verify against that. Invalidating the approval instead is safe but over-strict.

scenarios.title: CRM moves a customer to another office between approval and release
scenarios.rationale: A CRM office change moves that customer's collected revenue between branches by the CRM's authority (FI-6), not the mapping's; it does not change lead evidence or the current mapping, so release proceeds and its verification must not attribute the CRM move to itself (BR-8, FI-3).

expectFinal.notes: B35 -1056.00, B36 +1056.00 spend. k1's 175.00 is at B37 after the CRM move; company collected revenue stays 175.00.

scenarios.title: Fifteen contradicting calls arrive at the current branch after approval
scenarios.rationale: After approval, new calls make the evidence point back to B06 (15 vs 10), so the base the approver reviewed has moved; release must re-check, refuse, invalidate the approval and return the change to draft without moving anything (BR-7, BR-8, FI-4).

scenarios.title: Incident fix remaps the campaign through the old path after approval; re-preview, re-approve, release
scenarios.rationale: The current mapping moved (B24 -> B26) outside this tool after approval, so the approval no longer describes the base and release must be refused and invalidated (BR-7, BR-8); a fresh preview from B26 is routine again and its release moves spend from B26, not B24 (FI-2).

expectFinal.notes: The final release moves 747.60 from B26 to B25; B24 does not move during the release.

scenarios.title: More agreeing calls arrive after approval; the base still points the same way
scenarios.rationale: New calls at the proposed branch strengthen, not move, the evidence, and the current mapping is unchanged, so the base is the same and release must go through (BR-7, BR-8); refusing would be over-strict.

scenarios.title: All leads are corrected to another branch after the preview but before approval
scenarios.rationale: A person corrected all six leads from B20 to B21 after the preview, so the evidence the preview showed is stale; approving must be refused (BR-7), and a re-run preview now contradicts the evidence and must fail (BR-1, FI-4).

scenarios.title: A second change for the same campaign while the first is in review, and again while it is approved
scenarios.rationale: Two changes for the same campaign may not both be in review or approved (BR-12); the second and third proposals, though identical in content, must not reach ready_for_review while ch1 is open.

expectFinal.notes: ch2 and ch3 may be refused at request time or recorded without entering review; neither may be ready_for_review or approved.

scenarios.title: Two people release the same approved change at the same moment
scenarios.rationale: Release applies an approved mapping once (BR-8); exactly one release may succeed, and spend must move exactly once (FI-2), never doubled out of B01.

expectFinal.notes: B01 -2880.00 and B02 +2880.00 exactly once.

scenarios.title: Approver presents the identity of a different change under review (swap)
scenarios.rationale: An approval is bound to the exact configuration and preview reviewed (BR-7); presenting ch2's reviewed identity to approve ch1 must be refused, after which correct approvals of each still succeed.

scenarios.title: One approver rejects; a second approver then tries to approve and someone tries to release
scenarios.rationale: rejected is final (brief section 6); a later approval by another approver and any release must be refused, leaving the mapping untouched (FI-4).

scenarios.title: Author approves own change; a proposer without approve permission tries too
scenarios.rationale: Approval is by a different person with the approve permission, never the author (BR-6); both the engineer's self-approval and marketing's approval (no approve permission) must be refused, and only the approver's succeeds.

scenarios.title: Guest, B20 partner and Joshua's brand viewer try to propose a B20 mapping
scenarios.rationale: Proposing needs the propose permission and scope (BR-6); guest, partner (in scope but no permission) and brand (neither) must all be refused, while the same mapping from marketing is routine (BR-1).

expectFinal.notes: class ALLOW on refused proposals labels the mapping content (safe); the refusal is about the actor. g1, p1 and b1 must leave no change record that can be approved.

scenarios.title: Brand viewer approves a Joshua's change; approver tries to release; a second marketer releases
scenarios.rationale: The brand viewer is in scope but lacks approve permission, and the approver lacks the propose permission needed to release (BR-6, section 5); both must be refused, while release by marketing2 (propose permission, not the approver) is accepted.

scenarios.title: A different marketer resubmits someone else's blocked change
scenarios.rationale: Only the author may resubmit their own change (BR-13); marketing2's resubmission of marketing's change must be refused and must not supersede it, while the author's own corrected resubmission succeeds.

expectFinal.notes: After the refused ch2, ch1 must still be preflight_failed (not superseded) until ch3.

scenarios.title: After a verified release, an incident fix remaps the campaign back through the old path
scenarios.rationale: Monitoring checks the mapping is still in place (BR-9); once it has been changed outside the tool the change must become recovery_required, and nothing may be rolled back or re-applied automatically, so the live mapping stays where the outside change put it.

expectFinal.notes: No automatic rollback or re-apply: c1 stays at B21 until a person proposes a compensating change.

scenarios.title: Post-release calls arrive at the old branch; recovery needs a person-made compensating change
scenarios.rationale: Leads after release stop agreeing with the mapping (12 at B04 vs 2 at B05), so monitoring must move the verified change to recovery_required without rolling back (BR-9); the compensating proposal back to B04 faces split evidence and needs a person (BR-2).

expectFinal.notes: Release moved 1496.40 B04 -> B05; it must not be reversed automatically. ch2 is allowed because ch1 is final (BR-12 does not block it).

scenarios.title: Monitoring right after release with no new leads, then again once agreeing leads arrive
scenarios.rationale: With no post-release leads the system has nothing to confirm and must not claim verification or a business improvement (BR-2, BR-10); once agreeing leads arrive, monitoring verifies the change (BR-9).

expectFinal.notes: The day-26 monitor may leave the change in monitoring or degraded, never recovery_required. No step may report a CAC or revenue improvement (BR-10).

scenarios.title: Monitoring is requested on changes that were never released
scenarios.rationale: Monitoring only exists after release (brief section 6); running it on a change in review or approved must be refused and must not change its status.

scenarios.title: Campaign mapped to Mission B28 whose calls all land at Moxie B05
scenarios.rationale: Evidence supports B05, but the campaign's current mapping is Mission, so the move crosses brands and is never routine (BR-3); blocking would ignore the evidence (BR-1), so only a person who knows the campaign's ad account can decide.

expectFinal.notes: The preview must flag the Mission -> Moxie brand change; ALLOW is wrong. BLOCK is safe but over-strict.

scenarios.title: PMax successor with no leads of its own, proposed to its predecessor's Mission branch
scenarios.rationale: Lineage is context for a reviewer, not lead evidence (brief section 2); the successor itself has no leads, so the system cannot decide and must flag the missing evidence while showing the predecessor's mapping (BR-2).

scenarios.title: Mission lead-ads campaign spread three ways across B27, B28 and B29; reviewer rejects
scenarios.rationale: No branch has a majority (5 / 4 / 4 across calls and forms), so the system cannot pick one (BR-2); it must send the change to a person with the split shown, and a rejection must leave the campaign unmapped (FI-4).
